skill.name: toon-format
skill.description: Guides AI assistants to encode, validate, and repair structured data using Token-Oriented Object Notation for compact LLM prompts.
skill.summary: Create compact, validated TOON representations of structured data for LLM workflows.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown notation, data examples, documentation links, or harmless output redirection. Three findings confirm instructions to execute an unpinned npm CLI and local repair scripts, creating supply-chain and file-modification risks.

remediation.issue: Validation uses npx with an unpinned package reference.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed CLI version and require user confirmation before npx installs or executes the package.

remediation.issue: Automatic repair can execute local scripts that modify user files.
remediation.suggestion: Disable automatic repair by default, verify script provenance, preview affected files, and require confirmation before modifications.

content.value_statement: JSON can consume excessive prompt tokens when records repeat the same keys. This skill converts suitable structures into compact TOON and validates format rules.
actual_capabilities: Encodes key-value objects, arrays, and uniform records using TOON syntax.
Designs compact tabular layouts with explicit row counts and column names.
Applies indentation, delimiter, quoting, and array-termination rules.
Compares TOON with JSON to determine whether conversion is appropriate.
Provides CLI and repair workflows for validating TOON files.
limitations: TOON is less suitable for deeply nested or irregular data.
The skill does not provide the referenced repair scripts.
Validation requires an external npm CLI that may need installation.
Token savings vary with data shape and should not be treated as guaranteed.

use_cases.title: Compact Prompt Records
use_cases.description: Convert repeated business records into a tabular TOON representation for lower prompt overhead.

use_cases.title: Build Documentation Indexes
use_cases.description: Create compact indexes containing paths, summaries, priorities, and search terms for LLM retrieval.

use_cases.title: Validate Data Exports
use_cases.description: Review generated TOON files for counts, indentation, delimiters, and termination before pipeline use.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Simple Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these uniform records to TOON. Include explicit array counts, two-space row indentation, and a blank line after each table: [paste records]
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion of a small uniform list

prompt_templates.title: Choose TOON or JSON
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this data structure and choose TOON or JSON. Explain the choice, then encode it when TOON is suitable: [paste structure]
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the appropriate representation before conversion

prompt_templates.title: Repair Invalid TOON
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this TOON text for count, indentation, comment, delimiter, multiline, and termination errors. Return corrected TOON and summarize each correction: [paste text]

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Prompt Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign this dataset for compact TOON transport. Preserve every value, minimize repeated keys, identify lossy choices, and provide a validation checklist: [paste dataset]
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced schema optimization with fidelity checks

output_examples.input: Three user records with identical id, name, and role fields.
output_examples.output: A three-row TOON table with explicit count, named columns, two-space indentation, and a terminating blank line.

output_examples.input: A deeply nested configuration containing irregular objects and optional fields.
output_examples.output: A recommendation to retain JSON because the structure is not uniform and receives little benefit from tabular encoding.

output_examples.input: A TOON table with a missing count, unindented rows, and comma-separated nested values.
output_examples.output: A corrected table with an explicit count, indented rows, semicolon-separated nested values, and a concise correction summary.

best_practices: Keep JSON as the canonical source and use TOON for LLM transport.
Prefer tabular encoding for records that share a stable schema.
Validate counts, indentation, delimiters, and blank-line termination before use.
anti_patterns: Do not force deeply nested or irregular structures into TOON.
Do not place commas inside tabular cells when they represent nested values.
Do not run unpinned validators or repair scripts without reviewing and confirming execution.

faq.question: What is TOON?
faq.answer: TOON is Token-Oriented Object Notation, a compact text representation designed for structured data in LLM prompts.

faq.question: When should I use TOON instead of JSON?
faq.answer: Use TOON for uniform records and repeated schemas. Keep JSON for deeply nested, irregular, or tool-managed data.

faq.question: Does TOON always reduce token usage?
faq.answer: No. Savings depend on the data shape, tokenizer, and amount of repeated structure.

faq.question: How are arrays represented?
faq.answer: Arrays use explicit counts. Uniform object arrays can also declare column names and use indented tabular rows.

faq.question: How can I validate TOON output?
faq.answer: Use a trusted, pinned TOON parser or CLI. Review installation and execution before running external packages.

faq.question: Can this skill repair invalid TOON?
faq.answer: It can identify and suggest common corrections. Referenced automatic repair scripts are external to this skill and require separate review.
